clue.text: Building of road in US 21

indicators.note: building something means putting its parts together into a new structure, so the words that follow are assembled afresh

parts.note: the three words taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Road construction in America described as hopelessly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 points to the answer at 21-down, SQUARE, in its sense of an old fogey; 'US' belongs to the letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is slang for a person stuck in outdated ways, just as a square is someone hopelessly conventional.

clue.text: Dogs, say, in setters and labradors, energetic initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: first letters of in, setters, labradors, energetic; 'and' is skipped as a joining word

explanation.surface: Talk of dogs, and the setters and labradors among them being lively at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of east London on a bend of the Thames, so 'Dogs' is an example of an isle, not a pack of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a London peninsula, so 'Dogs, say' is one example of an island name.

clue.text: 21, location of 21 in NY?
21 hole through which seen architectural feature

indicators.note: something seen through a hole sits within its opening, so one piece is framed by the other

parts.note: a sty is a filthy place, as in 'this room is a hole'
an arch is a curved structure over an opening

explanation.surface: A gap in a wall offers a view of some piece of architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is SQUARE, meaning stiffly conventional; ARCH sits inside STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy describes stiff, formal, prim behaviour, the same buttoned-up quality called square.

clue.text: Top off container, one pulling on handle quicker?

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, with 'off' read as 'of'

parts.note: the opening letter of container
an invented word for someone working a lever

explanation.surface: Taking the lid off a jar, someone tugging the handle faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that LEVERER is a made-up agent noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicker in the sense of quick-witted, a sharper and more intelligent mind.

clue.text: 100% likely to break in for example?

indicators.note: in places the phrase before it inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: e.g. is the Latin abbreviation, exempli gratia
something very thin is fragile

explanation.surface: Asking whether a full hundred per cent chance of a break-in is a fair example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred per cent means the whole lot, every part with nothing left out.

clue.text: Cotton on cut that's bandaged in hospital

indicators.note: a bandage wraps around a wound, so the shortened word goes around the next piece
cut means the phrase is docked, losing its final letter

parts.note: to cotton on or click is to suddenly understand
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cotton wool applied to a cut that's dressed in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton' looks like a medical dressing, but 'Cotton on' is the phrasal verb for grasping something.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical facility, a place for treatment like a small hospital department.

clue.text: Wasted daughter in prison?

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young daughter
pent means penned up, shut in

explanation.surface: A girl locked up, perhaps after a drunken night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' tempts as slang for drunk, which suits the surface, but it is the sense of squandered.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent describes time or money squandered foolishly, as in a misspent youth.

clue.text: 21 from both sides?
100, 21 figure

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
1 is a square number, the square of itself

explanation.surface: A list of numbers ending in a figure, like a scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is SQUARE, and one is a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a solid geometrical shape, and figure is the geometric term for such a shape.

clue.text: Saucy always in Irish musical

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: Rent is a Broadway rock musical
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: An Irish stage show is cheeky all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is the Jonathan Larson rock musical about young artists in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy means cheeky and disrespectful, which is exactly what irreverent conveys.

clue.text: Message from berth in pub, perhaps, something sharp

indicators.note: in places the word before it within the word that follows

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a berth is a bed on a ship or train
a wire is a telegram

explanation.surface: A text sent by someone sleeping in a pub turns out to be cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'berth in pub' as a bed kept in a bar; the message then comes after it. A wire is an old word for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbed wire is fencing studded with sharp points, so it is a prickly, sharp thing.

clue.text: Fat cat sees gerbil with ague shivering

indicators.note: shivering is shaking about, so the letters are jumbled out of order

parts.note: the two nouns taken letter for letter; 'with' just joins them

explanation.surface: A cat watches a feverish pet rodent trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat cat' looks like an animal in a pet scene, but it is the slang for a wealthy, powerful person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a rich, important figure, and a big leaguer is someone operating at the top level.

clue.text: Ship's biscuit in tricky way

parts.note: hard means difficult
a tack is a course or approach, as in 'try a different tack'

explanation.surface: A sailor's biscuit served up in an awkward manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack is the dry, long-keeping biscuit eaten on old sailing ships.

clue.text: Vessel's end of week scandal?

parts.note: Friday is the end of the working week, abbreviated FRI
-gate is the suffix tacked on to scandals, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A ship caught up in a weekend scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a warship, a type of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Their names are forgotten, taking nighties off

definitions.note: a clause standing for the plural noun: things whose names escape us

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: nightdresses, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: People whose names are forgotten undressing for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thingies is what we call objects or people when we cannot recall their proper names.

clue.text: Entertainer, i.e. star, lead in theatre performing?

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act, so the letters are reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of theatre

explanation.surface: An entertainer, meaning a star, taking the lead in a theatre show.
explanation.definitionFit: Artiste is a word for a professional performer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: See 3
Hint: where to go in 21

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: 4 is a square number, two times two
the lav is the lavatory, where you go

explanation.surface: A tip on where to head within a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is SQUARE, and four is a square number, the square of two.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour of something is a hint or suggestion of it, a trace.

clue.text: Particular case with pile for sorting

indicators.note: something put out for sorting is to be rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the two nouns taken letter for letter; 'with' joins them

explanation.surface: A specific case set aside with a pile of papers to sort through.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is an old-fashioned adjective meaning special or particular.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the numbers one, four and nine are each a number times itself
second meaning: the answers at 1-down, 4-down and 9-across each mean old-fashioned, even or prim

explanation.walkthrough: The same numbers are read twice, first as plain integers and then as clue references; the question mark marks the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: One, four and nine are perfect squares, while dinosaur, starchy and level are all synonyms of square.

clue.text: Little bird impression made on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a signet ring leaves an impression in sealing wax

explanation.surface: A small bird imitated by a mimic on a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' suggests a mimic's act, but it means the mark made by a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so a little bird in the sense of a baby one.

clue.text: Semicircle and a 21 for setter, say

parts.note: the letter C is shaped like half a circle
taken as written
9 is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: Geometric bits handed to the crossword's compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 21-down is SQUARE; nine is a square number. 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog, so it is an example of a canine.

clue.text: Railway car where middle button pushed back to load posh goods, article squeezed in

indicators.note: pushed back means turned to run the other way
loading means taking something inside, so one piece holds the others
squeezed in means forced inside the letters already there

parts.note: the belly button sits in the middle of the body
U means upper-class
G stands for good, so several goods give a row of Gs
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rail carriage where a central button is pushed to load smart goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned-round belly button takes the posh letter and the goods after its first letter, with the article slipped between the last two of those goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage van is the carriage on a train set aside for passengers' bags.

clue.text: Reportedly something for fancy dress party individual, once?

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or spoken, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: a false hairpiece worn as part of a costume

explanation.surface: Someone at a costume party long ago wearing something to dress up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a fancy-dress do, but it is a political party; the Whigs were a British party that later became the Liberals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Whig was a member of an historical British political party, so a party member of former times.

clue.text: See 12 Across
Thread on the subject of OT woman

parts.note: re means regarding
Eve is the first woman in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A sewing thread discussed with reference to an Old Testament woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To reeve is a nautical verb: to pass a rope through a ring or hole, i.e. to thread it.

clue.text: Tunnel discovered, communist admits very afraid

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them inside
dis-covered means its covering is stripped away, so the outermost letters go

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
red is the colour of communism
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A tunnel is found, and a communist confesses to being very scared.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerved means rattled and lacking courage, so it fits being afraid.
